findings.finding: The `project.symbol-reference-completeness` criterion has `exec: "AGENT"` in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` but `execution_mode: single_turn` in the rubric front-matter (`.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-symbol-reference-completeness.md:5`). `build_descriptor` reads `exec` from routing (not from the prompt), so the criterion runs agentic at runtime – but the front-matter misleads prompt authors and any authoring/drift tooling into believing it is a single-turn criterion. The run log (committed at `docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md`) explicitly records that `exec: 1-TURN` silently produced 0 findings (run 2), proving the front-matter's declared mode is broken. No AC in the plan requires correcting the front-matter to `execution_mode: agentic`, and no automated test pins the alignment between routing `exec` and front-matter `execution_mode`.
findings.location: .rebar/criteria_routing.json line 12 (`"exec": "AGENT"`) vs .rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-symbol-reference-completeness.md line 5 (`execution_mode: single_turn`); AC5 and AC6 (no alignment test specified)
scenarios: A future prompt author reads the front-matter, concludes the criterion is single-turn, removes `exec: AGENT` from the routing to 'fix the inconsistency' – silently breaking the codebase search the rubric depends on and reverting the criterion to run-2 behaviour (0 findings).
A prompt-authoring or drift-checking tool flags the front-matter as inconsistent with the routing and 'corrects' the routing to `exec: 1-TURN`, again breaking the agent-tier search.
findings.suggested_fix: In `.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-symbol-reference-completeness.md`, change line 5 from `execution_mode: single_turn` to `execution_mode: agentic`. In the story's test file (`tests/unit/test_project_symbol_reference_completeness.py`), add an assertion that `routing["project.symbol-reference-completeness"]["exec"] == "AGENT"`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'independent, individually-shippable' claim in Approach with the hard C→A file dependency documented in Execution ordering — either drop 'independent' and say 'sequenced' or qualify it as 'independently valuable but sequenced for delivery'.
evidence: 'Three independent, individually-shippable changes. None of them is …'

'C (`06ae`) first — it creates the tracked `.claude/settings.json` AND the `.gitignore` negation that lets that one file be tracked while the rest of `.claude/` … stays ignored. Without that negation neither C's setting nor A's hook can be committed at all.'
Shared file + required negation means A has a hard dependency on C, which is the definition of non-independent.
findings.finding: The Approach section calls the three changes 'independent, individually-shippable' but the Execution ordering section establishes that story A cannot be shipped before story C because A 'only adds a hooks block to the file C created' and C also creates the .gitignore negation required for the file to be tracked at all. The two sections directly contradict each other on the independence property.
findings.location: Approach (paragraph 1: 'Three independent, individually-shippable changes') vs Execution ordering section ('C first — it creates the tracked .claude/settings.json AND the .gitignore negation … Without that negation neither C's setting nor A's hook can be committed at all')
scenarios: An implementer reading only the Approach might attempt to ship story A first, discover the file doesn't exist and can't be committed, and be confused about the plan's intent.
A reviewer grading story A as 'independently shippable' would reach the wrong conclusion about its pre-conditions.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Approach opening to: 'Three sequenced, independently valuable changes — each delivers a distinct structural fix, but they must land in the order C→D→A→B because A and C share `.claude/settings.json`.'  Remove 'individually-shippable' or replace with 'each shippable only after its declared predecessor'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge in the Approach section (item 2) that the coaching move's selection is controlled by the coach LLM, not the overlay, and that in practice the method coaching reaches agents via the hook (mechanism A) rather than via the review-time move — so mechanism B's demonstrated value is detection reliability, not coaching delivery.
evidence: Approach says: 'a project-only criterion + coaching move so that when a review finds source-code references were enumerated by hand (or incompletely), the agent is directed to re-derive them with Serena'

docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md: 'Across four agent-tier runs the coach never selected this move... there is no plan shape that fires this criterion without also firing a blocking built-in'
AC5 amendment: 'the move's APPEARANCE in a run's output is not achievable through the overlay — the overlay controls move applicability, the coach LLM controls selection'
Coaching-sample run log: move selected = 0 across all four agent-tier runs (runs 3, 4, 5 all show 'built-ins only' or moves 14/9/6, never the project move)
findings.finding: The Approach section presents mechanism B ('Coach it in-band when it is actually missed — a project-only criterion + coaching move') as solving the 'no trigger, no feedback' root cause, but the committed evidence (docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md, runs 3–7) demonstrates that the move is never selected by the coach LLM in practice: the same incomplete-inventory evidence fires the blocking built-ins G1G2/G6/E4 first, and Pass-4 coaches blocking findings before advisory ones, making the advisory move structurally last-in-line. There is no plan shape that produces the move's output without also triggering the blocking built-ins that pre-empt it. The Approach section does not disclose this, leaving a reader who stops at 'Approach' with a false expectation of what mechanism B delivers.
findings.location: Approach section, item 2 ('Coach it in-band when it is actually missed') — inconsistency with AC5 amendment and docs/serena-symbol-reference-coaching-sample.md §'The limitation this evidence establishes'
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer reading only the Approach section concludes mechanism B reliably coaches agents toward Serena at review time — it does not; the mechanism can only guarantee the move is OFFERED (in the applicable set), not SELECTED

A future contributor might 'strengthen' mechanism B (e.g. raise it to blocking) without understanding why it was deliberately advisory, because the structural constraint is disclosed only in AC5 and the evidence doc, not in the Approach
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach item 2, add a parenthetical such as: '(note: the move's appearance in a given run's output is coach-LLM selection, not overlay-controlled; in practice the method coaching reaches agents at call-time via the hook — mechanism B's distinct contribution is that the criterion fires reliably at review time, naming missed sites)'.
